claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if MRM mass production slips beyond 2026 (no shipping product by 1H27) or if reliability/yield reports contradict the pre-ramp BER claim.
claims.statement: TSMC's 200Gbps micro-ring modulator (MRM) built on the COUPE platform is scheduled to enter mass production later in 2026, with bit error rate below 1E-08 under process-controlled conditions reported ahead of ramp (third-party industry-media report citing Economic Daily News; production yield per se remains undisclosed by TSMC).

claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if capacity expansion is cancelled or materially delayed (e.g. 4Q26 capacity still near 2Q26 level), or if named customers publicly move CPO volume to another photonics foundry.
claims.statement: Institutional-investor estimates (via Commercial Times, relayed by TrendForce) quantify TSMC PIC/COUPE capacity ramp from ~500 wafers/month to 10,000 by 2Q26, 15,000 by 4Q26 and at least 25,000 by 2028, with NVIDIA, Broadcom and AMD as likely primary volume customers in 2026-2027 — a forward estimate of production scale, not measured shipments.

source_doc.permission_basis: Public TrendForce news article; canonical URL retained.
